translationRepairs: His wife, Lady Shi, was a younger sister of Gaozu's daughter.
Lady Shi, his wife, was a younger sister of Gaozu, the Jin emperor.
女弟 means Gaozu's younger sister; the existing English incorrectly makes her the sister of Gaozu's daughter.
His wife, the Lady Shi, was the younger sister of a daughter of Emperor Gaozu of Jin.
Lady Shi, his wife, was a younger sister of Gaozu, the Jin emperor.
The literal field contains the same mistaken kinship relation.
Before a reply came he hurried on the road. The court could not stop him, and he was at once appointed military governor of Yedu.
Before a reply came, he hurried onto the road. The court could not stop him, and he was at once appointed regent of Yedu.
鄴都留守 is the regent of Yedu, not a military governor; 'regent' matches this book's established rendering of 留守.
Before a reply came he hurried on the road. The court could not stop him, and he was at once appointed military governor of Yedu.
Before a reply came, he hurried onto the road. The court could not stop him, and he was at once appointed regent of Yedu.
The literal field likewise mistakes 留守 for a military governorship.
Zhongwei appeared before Gaozu in plain dress. Gaozu pardoned Zhongwei and appointed him acting Grand Tutor with concurrent appointments as Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat.
Zhongwei appeared before Gaozu in plain dress. Gaozu pardoned him and appointed him Honorary Grand Preceptor, Acting Grand Tutor, and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
The existing translation reverses 太師 and 太傅. The revised titles match the parallel Old History entry and this corpus's established terminology.
Zhongwei appeared before Gaozu in plain dress. Gaozu pardoned Zhongwei and appointed him acting Grand Tutor with concurrent appointments as Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat.
Zhongwei appeared before Gaozu in plain dress. Gaozu pardoned him and appointed him Honorary Grand Preceptor, Acting Grand Tutor, and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
檢校太師 is Honorary Grand Preceptor and 守太傅 is Acting Grand Tutor in the established Five Dynasties terminology.

After Gaozu died the death was kept secret. The ministers jointly executed Zhongwei and his sons Hongzhang, Hongcan, and Hongqiao. Their bodies were exposed in the market. Townspeople kicked and reviled them. Officers could not restrain them. The corpses were torn apart and trampled until in a moment nothing remained.

After Gaozu died the death was kept secret. The ministers jointly executed Zhongwei and his sons Hongzhang, Hongcan, and Hongsui. Their bodies were exposed in the market. Townspeople kicked and reviled them. Officers could not restrain them. The corpses were torn apart and trampled until in a moment nothing remained.
璲 is read sui; the third son's name is Hongsui, not Hongqiao.
When the Khitan invaded, the Deposed Emperor twice went in person to Chanzou. Du Zhongwei was northern campaign commander and Shouzhen was overall supervisor.
When the Khitan invaded, the Deposed Emperor twice went in person to Chanzhou. Du Zhongwei was northern campaign commander and Shouzhen was overall supervisor.
澶州 is Chanzhou; Chanzou is a typographical error.
When the Khitan invaded, the Deposed Emperor twice went in person to Chanzou. Du Zhongwei was northern campaign commander and Shouzhen was overall supervisor.
When the Khitan invaded, the Deposed Emperor twice went in person to Chanzhou. Du Zhongwei was northern campaign commander and Shouzhen was overall supervisor.
The literal field repeats the Chanzou typo for 澶州.
Supervising Ma Quanjie's army, he defeated Li Jinquan at Anzhou and was made commissioner of the palace secretariat for his merit.
Supervising Ma Quanjie's army, he defeated Li Jinquan at Anzhou and was made Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service for his merit.
宣徽使 is Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service, not an official of the Privy Council or palace secretariat.

Zhao Siwen had already rebelled at Jingzhao and sent someone with an imperial-yellow robe to Shouzhen. Shouzhen was greatly pleased, thinking heaven and men both responded. He raised troops, seized Tong Pass in the west, and recruited bandits, who rose everywhere.

Zhao Siwan had already rebelled at Jingzhao and sent someone with an imperial-yellow robe to Shouzhen. Shouzhen was greatly pleased, thinking heaven and men both responded. He raised troops, seized Tong Pass in the west, and recruited bandits, who rose everywhere.
綰 is read wan; the name is Zhao Siwan.
Shi reached Binzhou. The prefect supported him with troops. Military Governor Li Zhou of Bin retained him, sent fast riders to report the matter, and an edict exiled Shi to Shangzhou.

Shi reached Yanzhou, whose prefect gave him troops for protection. Li Zhou, military governor of Binzhou, detained Shi, sent swift riders to report the matter, and received an edict exiling Shi to Shangzhou.
The source separates 衍州 from 邠州. A corrupt 門 has replaced punctuation in the local Chinese text; it does not mean that troops escorted Shi toward a gate.
The mother of Prince Yanshu, Lady Ding of Chu, was beautiful. Yanze sent men to request her from the Empress Dowager. When the Empress Dowager hesitated, he seized her by force.
The mother of Prince Yanxu, Lady Ding of Chu, was beautiful. Yanze sent men to request her from the Empress Dowager. When the Empress Dowager hesitated, he seized her by force.
煦 is read xu; the prince's name is Yanxu.
